title: Without works of the law we are also sanctified—same Pauline sense as justification
source_text: XLI. Denique quemadmodum saepius dicit Apostolus nos sine operibus legis justificari, ita non minus vere, & ad Apostoli stylum accommodate, dicere possumus nos sine operibus legis sanctificari. Nam per opera legis Apostolus intelligit talem legis observationem, quae divinae gratiae necessitatem excludat, & cui merces reddenda sit, secundum debitum, non secundum gratiam; juxta illud ante citatum, Ei autem qui operatur, merces non imputatur secundum gratiam, sed secundum debitum. Item, Si ex operibus, jam non est gratia: quandoquidem opus jam non est opus. Adeoque ex operibus legis justificari, est eam praestitisse legi obedientiam, cui vita debeatur, juxta legis promissa; & ratione cujus, ex pacto foederis legalis, in Dei judicio, ab omni poena absolvi quis debeat. Justificari vero sine operibus legis, est in judicio divino absolvi, & ab omni reatu immunem pronunciari, eum quem lex reum peragit, quique non id legi praestitit obsequium, ut juxta legis rigorem absolvi mereatur. Jam vero quis non videt hoc sensu nos quoque sine legis operibus sanctificari. Nec enim, ut sancti apud Deum habeamur & simus, requiritur ut legi divinae, secundum totum ejus rigorem, satisfecerimus, & si ad eam akribeian, quam foedus operum exigit, simus examinandi, nullo modo in legem peccasse reperiamur. Sed quemadmodum Deus a reatu absolvit impium, id est, eum quem lex peccati arguit & convincit, dummodo fide viva & efficaci Christi meritum amplectatur: sic quoque illum in quo reperitur fides per charitatem operans, tanquam vere sanctum & justum probat atque agnoscit, licet alioqui legem saepius transgressus sit, & deficiat in multis, quae necessaria essent, in eo qui ex legali foedere, sanctus & justus pronunciandus esset.
pass_a_gloss: Finally just as the Apostle often says that we are justified without works of the law, so no less truly, and fittingly to the Apostle's style, we can say that we are sanctified without works of the law. For by works of the law the Apostle understands such observation of the law as excludes the necessity of divine grace, and to which a wage is to be rendered according to debt, not according to grace; according to that cited before, But to him who works, the wage is not imputed according to grace but according to debt. Likewise, If of works, then it is no longer grace: since the work is no longer a work. And so to be justified of works of the law is to have rendered to the law that obedience to which life is owed according to the promises of the law; and by reason of which, from the pact of the legal covenant, one ought in God's judgment to be absolved from every penalty. But to be justified without works of the law is to be absolved in the divine judgment, and pronounced immune from all guilt, him whom the law convicts as guilty, and who has not rendered to the law that obedience so as to deserve to be absolved according to the rigor of the law. Now who does not see that in this sense we also are sanctified without works of the law? For it is not required, that we may be held and be holy before God, that we have satisfied the divine law according to its whole rigor, and if we are to be examined by that exact observation of the law which the covenant of works demands, that we be found in no way to have sinned against the law. But just as God absolves the ungodly from guilt—that is, him whom the law of sin argues and convicts—provided he embraces Christ's merit with living and efficacious faith: so also he approves and acknowledges as truly holy and just him in whom is found faith working through charity, although otherwise he has often transgressed the law and fails in many things that would be necessary in one who according to the legal covenant would have to be pronounced holy and just.
pass_b_english: As we are justified without works of the law, so we are sanctified without them—same debt-vs-grace sense.
God counts living charity-working faith holy despite legal shortfalls—parallel to forensic absolution of the guilty believer.
